description: Cross-slice compatibility review for the frozen ACCORD-02A/B/C/D candidate stack.

entries.basis: The same principal identifier names the issuer, subject, observer, dispatcher, or actor across slices.
Grant identity is reused for authority analysis and effect linkage.
Intent remains the logical requested-goal identity.
Task identity is logical and stable across retries.
Delegation edge identity is reused while delegation kind remains explicit.

entries.linkage: effect_id as logical effect across A/B/C/D
entries.basis: Effect identity remains stable across concrete attempts.
Every retry is required to have a distinct attempt identity.
C carries observation references through evidence and record references rather than requiring observation_id as a result field.
Evidence identifiers are retained in admissibility, binding, observation, and result records.
Provider operation identifiers are external correlation values and must remain non-authoritative.
A/C require verifier_run_id while D requires experiment run_id and does not require a verifier_run_id field or a typed reference.
D result_ref is an unconstrained string and does not require an A/C result schema or result_id lineage.

entries.linkage: predicate_id and stage to A portable records
entries.basis: C requires predicate/stage-aware targets, but A has no first-class effect predicate record and D does not require predicate/stage on every attempt/evidence link.

entries.linkage: A grant/delegation records into B relation analysis
entries.basis: B explicitly consumes A grant, delegation, task, intent, and effect links.

entries.linkage: B aggregate_relation into C/D authority axis
entries.basis: B grant relation is not the same semantic dimension as C/D authority validity, but D uses one relation_or_state carrier.

entries.linkage: B effective_authority.state into C/D authority axis
entries.basis: CONTAINED, POSSIBLE_WIDENING, and WIDENED effective states are not AUTHORIZED or INVALID_AUTHORITY decisions.
B says it does not authorize dispatch; no normative source or mapping supplies C/D event-time validity statuses.

entries.linkage: B comparison profile and C settlement profile
entries.basis: Both profiles are explicit, but their outputs cannot be compared without retaining profile identity.

entries.linkage: B revocation/expiry observations into C event-time authority
entries.basis: C has event-time authority axes and B requires supplied temporal validity observations.

entries.linkage: B transport non-authority invariant into D transports
entries.basis: Both prohibit transport metadata from creating or widening authority.
D copies the C occurrence vocabulary and keeps it separate from attribution and causality.
D uses the C attribution states.
D uses the C causality states.
D uses the C freshness states.
D uses the C duplicate-diagnostic states.

entries.linkage: C profile compatibility into D profile_compatibility
entries.basis: D uses the C compatibility values.

entries.linkage: C result_id referenced by D result_ref
entries.basis: A string reference can carry the C result identity, but D does not type-check it.
A result kind is a wrapper label while C separates occurrence, attribution, causality, freshness, duplication, and profile compatibility.
A describes a qualified observation and C defines profile-bounded non-occurrence; no normative mapping states when they coincide.
A lifecycle-oriented unknown labels are not directly mapped to C's multidimensional conclusion and reopening axes.

entries.linkage: C staged predicate into D experiment settlement
entries.basis: The prose preserves stages, but the D record and catalog do not require a typed stage mapping for every evidence and attempt path.

entries.linkage: A issued/attempted/observed times into C temporal profile
entries.basis: C profiles distinguish event, observation, issuance, verification, and current time; A supplies a subset of the record times.

entries.linkage: C event time versus observation time
entries.basis: The C model and schema explicitly preserve the distinction.
D result records carry the required experiment timing fields and can reference C event semantics.

entries.linkage: A evidence artifact trust root into C trust assumptions
entries.basis: A carries trust_root_id and C applies explicit observer/trust-root assumptions.

entries.linkage: C provenance/binding assessments into D observed evidence
entries.basis: D carries evidence and profile references, while C performs the detailed binding assessment.
A permits extensions and B/C profiles require explicit unknown handling rather than silent disappearance.
All reviewed slices deny transport metadata semantic authority.
Both are carriage profiles and the D matrix requires at least these two transport families.
A2A is defined as an optional conformance target and is not normatively required in the first scored core.

entries.linkage: portable bundle plus C profile/evidence as verifier input
entries.basis: The verifier can use exported records, profiles, trust roots, and evidence, subject to the missing identity/result translation.

entries.linkage: D scenario/run records linked to portable records
entries.basis: D task/effect identity records and record_refs can point into the A bundle.

entries.linkage: public scenario catalog versus hidden oracle
entries.basis: The catalog openly carries oracle_state and expected conformance bounds while D does not require a sanitized run-facing manifest.

entries.linkage: public scenario metadata versus baseline input boundary
entries.basis: Per-arm field allowlists are not machine-readable and baseline output is intentionally open-ended.
D declares scorer-only visibility and private_state_used=false, but physical separation must be frozen before implementation.

entries.linkage: ACCORD-02 claims versus ACCORD-01 prior-art boundary
entries.basis: This row is a review boundary, not a schema linkage.
The reviewed artifacts specify no runtime ownership transfer.
